A session is charged on the server clock from the mint to the last heartbeat; the client heartbeats every thirty seconds and counts down locally, ending the call itself when the minutes run out; a client that goes quiet is charged for its whol

commits.subject: The Magician on a phone: look with one finger while you walk
commits.lede: While a finger rested on the joystick the browser reported two active touches, and the look handler treated any two as a pinch, so you could not turn while you moved and looking felt like it needed two fingers. Only touches that began on the world count now. One finger looks anywhere on the world (the left-half drag-stick survives only on wide touch screens that have no joystick), a flick keeps turning for a moment a

commits.subject: The Magician in VR: pinch to talk, hold to leave, and a recorder
commits.lede: In the headset a trigger or a hand pinch now starts the conversation when no game is running (it still shoots during one), and holding it for two seconds ends the XR session, which is the only way out with bare hands. A pinch is button 0 on a hand's gamepad and was also bound to jump, which is why talking looked like jumping; jump is now only the face buttons on a controller. The strip under the view says what the tr

commits.subject: The Magician: left and right were swapped for every input
commits.lede: The player's 'right' vector was built as (fwd.z, 0, -fwd.x), which at yaw 0 is (-1, 0, 0): left. The joystick, the touch drag, the D key and the VR thumbstick all used it, so all four walked the wrong way sideways while forward and back were fine, which is why it read as an inverted stick rather than a broken one. It is (-fwd.z, 0, fwd.x) now, and a script drives the stick and the D key and checks the sign of x.

commits.subject: The Magician on a phone: a stick, a pinch, one menu
commits.lede: A phone is a different HUD, not a smaller one. Under 640 px the page shows a joystick (src/magician/ui/Joystick.tsx), a jump button, a shoot button during a game, and one menu that holds the companion picker, sound, hide, an invite button that shares the room link, and leave. The suggestion chips become one scrolling row and the footer goes; the transcript keeps two lines.

commits.subject: The Magician: play together, and a real wizard body
commits.lede: Multiplayer as broadcasting patches (src/magician/net.ts). The world is data, so a shared valley is every patch on a Supabase Realtime channel (?room=name, default hoshimura): say 'make it rain' and it rains for everybody. Presence at eight hertz draws the other players as ghosts (src/magician/world/peers.ts) with name tags and a talking ring. A newcomer says hi and the first full state it hears wins; there is no hos

commits.subject: The Magician: roster companions face the player, quieter robot eyes
commits.lede: Verified at noon with the sun behind the camera: the Quaternius roster faces the same way as the robot. The earlier flip made them face away; what had looked like a back at golden hour was a face in its own shadow. The robot's lenses glow at a fraction of what they did. A debug hook, window.__magician.companion(), lists the mounted body's meshes and materials for scripts.

commits.subject: The Magician: three games, any companion, headset clicks, sky props
commits.lede: Games (src/magician/game): Oni Siege, Spirit Lights and Dragon's Breath share one runner (enemies, bolts, hearts, a shield and a blast that Vibey casts on request) and each mode is about 150 lines of rules. The world's tools are the weapons: rain drowns fire oni, snow slows them, a storm's lightning strikes them, a flood drowns them, fog hides the player from the yurei, lit lanterns keep it away. Vibey aims at the ne

commits.subject: The Magician: merge the fixed forest into a few meshes for the headset
commits.lede: 260 trees built one at a time were about 1,700 meshes. The fixed forest is now one merged geometry per species (so the season still recolours each species through its one material) plus one for all the trunks: five draw calls. Conjured trees are still individual and still sway.

Ten weeks off-grid near the Salton Sea, ridden on an electric unicycle across a pale desert with the sea a silver line to the west, low mountains east, six camps of pallet racks, plywood, shade cloth and solar around one table, Poop Mountain, a wireframe dodecahedron at Mars Research, and Bombay Beach a couple of minutes' ride away with Sunflower Lab and the

One eight-minute day from 4 pm to 8:30: a secret meetup location is drawn per run,

commits.lede: A new world at /agentocracy (aliases /cardboard-city, /bainbridge). Three true things at once: the Agent Village governance experiment at Edge Esmeralda, the kids' cardboard city from the same month, and Bainbridge Island, where Jack grew up.

commits.lede: Lake Chelan, September 6, 2025: a first-person Olympic-distance triathlon whose whole idea is that you cannot see. The goggles fog a little more with every stroke, orange turn buoys blur into blobs, kayaks splash at the course edge, and the churn of swimmers at the start costs you mouthfuls. Breathe on the beat and not into a wave, or the Lake Chelan ingested percentage ticks up; hold Q to stop and clear the lens for

commits.lede: Real captures from each running world: Vibey on the Dipsea trail with the ghost runners, Pathfinder on the mast at Moffett with the Bay behind her, month 25 of a Healdsburg build in two inks, and the party from under the duck. `npm run stamp` dates all four. The Long Silence's passport panel capped its list at 42 rows and these made 46, so the cap moves to 48, which is still inside the band where the type does not sh

commits.subject: Four worlds from one week: the Dipsea, Pathfinder, Developer Trail, Duck On My Head
commits.lede: A trail run over Mount Tam with the real Dipsea profile under your feet, a 406-foot rigid airship making relief drops around the Bay, an Oregon Trail for a nine-lot cottage project, and a house party seen from a robot with a rubber duck on its head. Each is a thin page plus an engine directory, one registry entry, and a passport stamp. Card art follows in the next commit.

commits.lede: `lib/screen.ts` is the one answer to "is this a phone" — the shorter side under 520 px — plus touch and orientation, for every HUD that has to ask.

commits.lede: The locker preview and the in-game skin both fitted characters from a bounding box, and no box is honest for every rig in the catalog: the Quaternius armatures draw from their bones at twice their bind box, the Esmeralda pirates box at twice their drawn size. `refitByRender` draws the rig once, flat white, into a small offscreen target and reads the alpha back; both the preview and `play/skin.ts` rescale and re-plant

commits.lede: A locker on every royale entry screen — the roster shared with the city and the profile, the shop's tiers and locks, the island's own drop suit first — and a skin system that loads the pick through the same `loadCharacterRig` every other world uses and mounts it over the drop-suit actor, which keeps simulating underneath. Portraits for the GLB half of the roster, photographed by the same script that shoots the code-b

commits.subject: dz-play/dz-shot: join DZ_ROUTE's query correctly
commits.lede: A route that already carries a query (`/drop-zero?mode=classic`) was getting `?shot=1` appended after it, so `shot` became part of the previous value and the page never signalled ready. The classic regression run sat for three minutes and exited. Join with `&` when there is already a `?`.

commits.subject: BETTER FORTNITE: eat the augment digit in fixed(), harness filter, card art
commits.lede: The inventory latches edge input in its own `fixed()`, and the engine runs every system's fixed pass before any update — so consuming `input.slot` in `update` was always one step late, and the playtest recorded a pick that also switched the player to the pickaxe. The consume moves to `fixed`; augments is first in the boot list precisely so it runs before the inventory's. The beat now asserts the active slot did not m

commits.subject: BETTER FORTNITE: a third game on the island (checkpoint)
commits.lede: Drop Zero's bullets and health plus the four things a battle royale is missing — augments picked mid-match, a grapple on every hip, a second wind after the first down, and an island that does things while the circle closes. One page, one engine, `mode: "better"`; four new systems that boot only there, and every other system reads their services lazily and treats absence as the classic answer.

commits.subject: The real weather, and a painted mountain on Twin Peaks
commits.lede: /sf now opens in whatever San Francisco is actually doing. Open-Meteo, no key, one GET; `src/sf/weather/report.ts` turns the reply into rain, ground fog, haze, fog density and a wind vector, and `Weather.tsx` eases the world onto it over half a minute. If Karl is in off the Pacific this afternoon, he is in here too.

commits.subject: The day passes now, and you can wave at people
commits.lede: Four small things, and one of them was hiding behind the others.

commits.subject: Other people are in San Francisco now
commits.lede: Open /sf and you are in it with everybody else who has it open: as your own Vibeverse character, with your name over your head, walking the same Market Street. If somebody gets into a car, you see a car.

commits.subject: Stroll is the default. The loud version is a button.
commits.lede: Four things came back from playing it and all four were right: blurry, chaotic, dead on mobile, and it took a machine down. Every one of them traces to the same mistake — I made the heaviest thing the *default* and left the calm thing nowhere.

commits.subject: A way back to first person, and a hint that says how to get in a car
commits.lede: Third person is the right default for this world and it was a one-way door: the boom went out on mount and nothing brought it back. `T` now swaps (not `V`, which every third-person game in the world uses and which the wingsuit already has here). The prop is the starting view; the player owns it after that. The viewmodel follows, so the arms come back with the eyes.

commits.subject: Tame the lens, and two determinism bugs the fog change flushed out
commits.lede: **The lens.** With the post chain on, driving into the sun put a blown white blob and a rainbow arc across the car. That is not the sun — the flare's ghost image is the thresholded frame inverted through the optical axis, so a bright sky at the *top* of the screen lands at the *bottom* of it, which in a third-person game is exactly where the vehicle you are driving is. At the authored strength it read as a rendering

commits.subject: Turn the post chain on, and thin Karl out
commits.lede: The last unmounted subsystem. `Pipeline` subscribes to the frame at priority 1, which is React Three Fiber's signal to stop rendering by itself and hand presentation over, so mounting it changes how every pixel gets to the screen: ambient occlusion, screen-space reflections, volumetrics, TAA, bloom and the ACES grade instead of a straight forward render. Every pass is behind the quality tier, and `detectQualityTier`

commits.subject: The crowd is from San Francisco now, not from nowhere
commits.lede: Everybody on every pavement in the city was one uniform pick from a list of seven: three civilians, a slim one, a heavy one, a tourist, a construction worker. The Marina at ten in the morning had the same seven people as the Tenderloin at midnight, and since you spend a walking game looking *along* the pavement rather than up at the facades, the crowd is most of what tells one neighbourhood from another at street lev

commits.subject: The Legos were parked cars and distant trees
commits.lede: Two different things at street level both read as coloured bricks floating about, and neither was a placement bug — every object was exactly where it should be. They were both silhouette bugs.

commits.subject: The city was already built. Nothing had turned it on.
commits.lede: Seventy-nine thousand lines of San Francisco — vehicles, crowds, traffic, police, weapons, physics, missions, audio, the whole HUD — sat in `src/sf` importing each other and imported by nothing. The composition root mounted six static components and a walker. Every one of those subsystems documents its own integration in its header ("Mount it once inside the Canvas"), every one typechecks, and 113 tests across nine s

commits.subject: Write down the night's four features and its two worst lessons
commits.lede: The card was taken before the skybridges went back in, before there was a camp on the ice and before anything happened after dark. `npm run stamp` reads each world's `source` to work out when it last changed and that date is on every card in the hub, so it has to be run after a night like this one or every card lies by a day.

commits.subject: You can ride the ring tram, and a moving floor is now a primitive
commits.lede: `traffic.ts` has run a real tram on the middle ring road since the world was built — a lap in ninety seconds, four stops — and its own header said, in as many words, that it deliberately implemented no interaction and whatever owned the player could do the rest. `interiors.ts` even put a bench at Halo Station labelled "Wait for the tram". Nobody built the rest.

commits.subject: The camera rig allocated two vectors a frame
commits.lede: `CameraRig.update` runs every frame and the house rule for every per-frame path in this world is that it must not allocate — a dozen systems each handed a fresh object sixty times a second is a garbage-collector pause you can see, and it is why the frame context is one object mutated in place rather than a new one.

commits.subject: The black rectangle was one NaN, and four rooms somebody lives in
commits.lede: ## The rectangle

commits.subject: A camp on the ice, a festival after dark, a camera, and the bridges back
commits.lede: Four things landed together. All of it is verified on a clean checkout rather than on the tree it was written in — four agents were writing to that tree at once, and a route that navigates while Vite swaps its own chunks comes back with an "Invalid hook call" and the crash screen, which looks exactly like a regression and is not one.

commits.subject: Ignore __scratch_* too, which is the pattern that lands inside src/
commits.lede: Five of these have accumulated, each added the morning after a scratch file turned up in a commit. This one matters more than the others because it is the only one that lands *inside* a source directory: a throwaway `src/empyrean/__scratch_cost.ts` is on the typecheck path, and one careless `git add -A` puts it on a live `main`.

commits.subject: A dead browser is a fact about the harness, not ten broken worlds
commits.lede: `npm run smoke` opens a hundred routes in one Chromium and about eighty of them raise a WebGL context under a software rasteriser, so sooner or later that process dies. When it did, `browser.newPage()` rejected from outside the per-route try: node printed a raw stack, exited 1, and printed no summary, no tally and no list of the routes it never reached.

commits.subject: Stamp the dates and regenerate the build log
commits.lede: `npm run stamp` reads each world's `source` to work out when it last changed, and that date is on every card in the hub — so it has to be run after a change to a world's code or every card lies by a day.

commits.subject: Twice as many people, and 334 benches that finally have somebody on them
commits.lede: The Halo was empty and nobody could work out why, because it looks like a plaza and a plaza is walkable. It is: `buildNav` simply puts zero nav nodes inside `HALO_R`. One ring at r=62 and nothing across it, so the pathfinder had no way to route anybody over the biggest open space in the city, and the Beacon — which asked for ten people standing in front of it — got none, because the nearest node was 24 m off its 38 m

commits.subject: Ignore .scratch/ anywhere, which is the general case
commits.lede: Four separate patterns have accumulated in this part of `.gitignore` and each was added the morning after a scratch file turned up in a commit — including one of mine last night, when `git add -A` swept three of an agent's throwaway tests into a commit about the sky. A directory named `.scratch`, at any depth, is the general case rather than a fifth prefix to guess at.

commits.subject: Recapture the card, stamp the dates, regenerate the build log
commits.lede: The card was taken before the towers became glass and before there was a spaceport on the horizon. `npm run stamp` reads each world's `source` to work out when it last changed, and that date is on every card in the hub — so it has to be run after a night like this one or every card lies by a day.

commits.subject: The Meridian: a tower you walk into, ride up, and stand on top of
commits.lede: Twenty-three towers in the Spires and not one of them had an inside. `spire.ts` builds a single tower end to end — curtain-walled shell, double-height lobby, a scenic lift that really travels, and a belvedere with a cantilevered glass floor you can stand on and see the street three hundred metres straight down through.

commits.subject: Families, children, dogs and robots — and benches that know which way they face
commits.lede: Eight hundred and twenty people were eight hundred and twenty individuals transiting. Now about seventy-seven of them are families, ninety-two are couples, thirty are walking a dog, and there are twenty-eight civic robots — five sweepers working a kerb, eleven couriers with a parcel, twelve companions that go and stand next to the *child* when a group stops.

commits.subject: Lead the onboarding with the thing you can see, and photograph the spaceport
commits.lede: The opening line named sunmotes scattered all over the island and the Launch Terrace. Both are true and neither is in front of you. There is now an aircraft parked on a lit pad twenty metres up the avenue from where you arrive, and getting into it is one keypress — so that is the line. A first sentence that names something visible and actionable in three seconds is worth three that describe the world.

commits.subject: Give the whole-world builds room, now that the world is bigger
commits.lede: Three tests build the entire world — every building, every interior, eight hundred props, the crowd, the traffic, and now seven aircraft and a spaceport — and two of them started overrunning vitest's five-second default the moment it grew. Both failed on a timeout rather than an assertion, which reads as "the world is broken" and is the most expensive false alarm this repository can raise. Thirty seconds each, matchi

commits.subject: Warn before the launch, not after it, and write down the two new systems
commits.lede: A rocket you are told about once it has lit is a rocket you missed. The countdown toast now fires at T-44 and says which way to look; the second one still counts the *sound* rather than the ignition, because from the plaza that is 5.9 seconds late and the delay is the most convincing thing about watching a launch from two kilometres away.

commits.subject: Aircraft on the roofs, a spaceport on the horizon, and a playground
commits.lede: Three things, and the two big ones were built in parallel by agents against the contract in `types.ts`.

commits.subject: An uncaught exception is a smoke failure, however much got drawn first
commits.lede: Tonight I pushed a half-written module to a branch that deploys. `/empyrean` threw `flyerParts is not defined` out of its vehicle builder partway through booting, and `npm run smoke` printed

commits.subject: Write down the skybridge attempt, since the failure outlived the code
commits.lede: Nine glass tubes between tower crowns, chosen off the built lots. Rendered, the city grew one screen-filling near-black rectangle occluding everything in a forty-degree cone — and it survived a complete rewrite of the geometry, from `boxAt` on the glass bucket to `prism` with the pen's base, span and seed set the way `buildLot` sets them. The artefact did not change at all when the geometry it supposedly came from ch

commits.subject: A moon you can believe, at the third size
commits.lede: The first one thresholded the dot product against 0.9993, which is four degrees across — eight moons wide — and with the halo on it the night sky had a searchlight in it. The dot product is the wrong quantity as well as the wrong number: cos is flat at zero, so every value that matters is within one part in a hundred thousand of 1.0 and the precision goes exactly where all the detail is. The chord between two unit ve

commits.subject: Back out an agent's half-written vehicles.ts that I pushed by accident
commits.lede: `git add -A src` while four subagents were mid-edit swept an unfinished `vehicles.ts` and three of their scratch test files into a commit about the sky, and I pushed it to a branch that deploys. `/empyrean` threw `flyerParts is not defined` out of `buildVehicles` before the world booted: a black screen on a live route, from a commit whose message is about the moon.

commits.subject: A moon, a blue hour, and a dusk that ends
commits.lede: Now that the hour is somebody's to choose, the hours have to be worth choosing, and two of them were not.

commits.subject: Regenerate the published build log
commits.lede: `prebuild` rewrites it on every `npm run build`, so it comes out of a verification run dirty and one commit behind. Regenerated against the tip so the copy served at myvibeverse.com/build-log.json matches what is on main.

commits.subject: Give the hour and the weather to the player
commits.lede: The world has had a full day cycle and five weather conditions since it was built, and until now the only thing that could reach either was a debug hook meant for a screenshot script. That is a strange thing to hide: the whole argument for a world painted at one specific minute of one specific sunset is that the light *is* the world, and moving it is five different places for the price of one.

commits.subject: Glass, rather than a painting of glass
commits.lede: The towers were a bright painted gradient with 12% environment mixed over them at face-on. That is what plaster looks like. Glass is the other way round — a dark body under a bright reflection — and three things were missing before it could be:

commits.subject: Bind the look drag where nothing can get above it
commits.lede: Jack cannot turn the camera by dragging — in this world *or* in Vibe Island, in an ordinary Chrome window, holding the left button. Two completely different bindings failing the same way says the fault is not in either one's arithmetic, so this stops relying on the part that can be taken away.

Note what the recorder actually measured, and that the prompts were walked
commits.lede: `route-gif` refused this world — four distinct frames against a floor of eight — and the honest reading is not "nothing moves here": every frame it captured was distinct, and it only got four because SwiftShader renders the Empyrean at about a frame a second. The recorder cannot tell an inert world from a slow rasteriser. The still stands, but the reason is written down.

commits.subject: Recapture the card, and stamp the dates
commits.lede: The card art was taken before the shopfronts were fixed, so it had the curtain of stretched glazing hanging under the island in it — which is the one part of the picture the card is *about*. The keel is a keel now.

commits.subject: Cut stone on the terrace faces, and a promenade you can see from
commits.lede: The wall you stand against on the promenade is a hundred metres of fascia two metres from the lens, and it was one flat mauve field with a soft vertical shimmer over it — a rhythm expressed as a 22% shading swing is a rhythm you can only read from a kilometre away. A retaining wall reads as masonry from three things: bays with real edges, courses across them, and a plinth and a cornice saying which way is up. All thr

commits.subject: Four hundred trees were black because green times green is not green
commits.lede: Every tree carries its leaf colour on `instanceColor`, and three multiplies that by the vertex colour — so tagging the canopy geometry green as well squared it: #4f8f4e rendered as #183618. In a city that is otherwise all warm light at dusk, four hundred black blobs along the avenues were the loudest wrong thing at street level, and the thing that looked wrong was the *shading*, which is in a different file.

commits.subject: The shopfronts were six hundred metres tall
commits.lede: `shopfront` takes a level and a height, and two of its four derived numbers confused the one for the other:

commits.subject: Step the nav graph by its clearance, not by a guess at a spacing
commits.lede: The crossing stitcher walked each candidate edge at a fixed interval and asked `surfaceAt` whether it was still on pavement. Five even samples let eighteen edges through a building; one every 1.2 m still let twenty through. commits.subject: Untrack the scratch harnesses agents leave behind
commits.lede: `.tmp-t.mjs` and `__zz_vshot.mjs` are one-off Playwright drivers written to look at a frame and then forgotten. They got swept into a commit by a `git add -A` while their author was still using them, which is how a throwaway becomes a file somebody has to wonder about in six months.

commits.subject: Two daylights, and a snowfield that fog could not touch
commits.lede: The lighting pass landed and it found two bugs it could not reach from its own files. Both were mine.

commits.subject: A budget on what the world costs, and a clock that dwells
commits.lede: **`src/test/empyreanBudget.test.ts`** counts draw calls and triangles per system and holds a ceiling on each. Frame rate cannot be measured here — no GPU, so Chromium rasterises on the CPU — but the numbers that *cause* frame rate can, and they are exact: they are what the page asks the driver to do, and they are identical on real hardware.

commits.subject: Unseal the café and the gallery; stop photographing the menu
commits.lede: Three things the last round turned up.

commits.subject: A test that catches the bugs a green build cannot
commits.lede: `src/test/empyreanWorld.test.ts` builds every system that does not need a renderer, steps it two frames, and looks for the failures whose symptom is a black screen rather than an exception:

commits.subject: The city is standing: ten systems, integrated, and it renders
commits.lede: Still on the branch, not main — the frames show real problems and it is not worth a live deploy yet. But it typechecks, builds, and opening `/empyrean` gives you a street with kerbs, lit windows, trees, benches, a tram, birds and a five-hundred-metre Beacon at the end of it.

commits.subject: WIP: the plan, and ten systems being built against it
commits.lede: Not on main, and not ready for it: this tree does not typecheck. `world.ts` imports systems that are still being written, and pushing it would take a live `main` down. It is here so the work is not sitting only in a container.

commits.subject: npm run stamp, and a lockfile a fresh clone can actually install
commits.lede: Two things, and the second one is the one that matters.

commits.subject: THE EMPYREAN: a glass city on a rock that never landed
commits.lede: A new world at /empyrean, built from a reference painting: a cluster of iridescent towers on a floating island four hundred metres over a frozen lake, in a sunset that runs navy-and-stars at the zenith through jade and gold to rose on the horizon. You fly it with Vibe City's jetpack, as whichever character you already picked anywhere else in the vibeverse.

commits.subject: Towers meet the ground now, and the card art stopped being a rooftop
commits.lede: Every generated tower ran as one banded box from the pavement to the parapet, which is a shape no tower has and the one part of it you stand next to. Walk down Market — where the world opens — and both sides were forty storeys of identical window courses meeting the ground with nothing at all: no lobby, no entrance, no way in, no change of material. It reads as scenery from six feet away, on the most-looked-at facade

commits.subject: npm run stamp
Streets that are lit at night, and headlights on the traffic
commits.lede: Nine thousand glowing window courses turned the skyline into San Francisco from the air the day they went in, and from the pavement the roads stayed a black void with a few bright dots floating over them — which is what a power cut looks like, not a city. Four things fix it.

commits.subject: build-log.json has been serving a merge conflict
commits.lede: `public/build-log.json` is published at myvibeverse.com/build-log.json, and the committed copy contains `<<<<<<< HEAD` and `=======` — a conflict resolved by committing both sides. It has not been parseable JSON since.

commits.subject: The lido's pools: water that behaves like water
commits.lede: They were a MeshStandardMaterial with a low roughness, an environment map and a constant alpha, which is physically reasonable and photographed as a flat sheet of turquoise paint. A perfectly flat surface with a static reflection has nothing in it that moves or that changes with angle, and those are the two things that say "water" before anything else does.

commits.subject: Document the lido and the ground probe; refresh stamps
commits.lede: The lido's boot position is load-bearing — it has to come up before props and vegetation, because neither knows the park is coming and both plant into open ground. Run it after them and there are trees in the wave pool. That was worth writing down next to the rest of the load order rather than leaving it as a line in boot.ts that looks reorderable.

commits.subject: dz-ground: ask the world what is under a dark pixel
commits.lede: Three captures came back with a large near-black field across the near and middle ground and correctly-lit terrain beyond it, and four different theories about it all predicted the same photograph: dark ground cover, a canopy underside, a shadow-map artifact and a metalness bug are indistinguishable in a frame. Two of the four were confidently wrong.

commits.subject: Drop Zero: give it back its home button
commits.lede: `AppChrome` decides whether a world owns the viewport by asking `CHROMELESS_ROUTES.has(pathname)`, and a pathname never carries a query. Drop Zero's registry route is `/drop-zero?mode=classic`, so the set held a string no URL could ever equal: the nav pill rendered over the crosshair, and — the worse half — the chromeless branch is also the branch that hands a fullscreen world its HomeButton, so the classic mode had

commits.lede: A separate realm in the same world: a municipal water park on the island's NE shelf. A 28 m tower of flumes into three splash pools, a wave pool with a shelving floor you can walk into, a 163 m lazy river whose current actually carries you, splash pads with a bucket always tipping, a diving stack, cabins, a kiosk, a car park, and twenty-two signs in one draw call. 1,319 colliders.
